verdict.rationale: Lium documents on-demand GPU provisioning through the CLI (`lium up --gpu H100`), the API (`POST /executors/rent-by-spec`) and a create-pod flow. It also documents running code on the pod right away via `lium exec`, the SDK and Jupyter. The openapi probe 404s only hit docs.lium.io paths, while the docs point to lium.io/api/openapi.json, so they do not contradict the API claim. Missing for 10: any evidence of actual time-to-running (the "within minutes" part), and independent or hands-on corroboration of the provisioning flow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can provision an on-demand GPU instance from the console or API and be running code on it within minutes

citations.quote: pip install lium.io && lium up --gpu H100 --ttl 1h
rent-by-spec (`POST /executors/rent-by-spec`) that rents the cheapest node matching a GPU spec under a `max_price_per_gpu_hour` ceiling
lium exec job "nvidia-smi"                              # exits with the remote command's exit code
The SDK rents the cheapest matching node, runs the function there, returns the result and removes the pod (or keeps it warm).
An agent can do everything on Lium with no browser: sign up, fund, rent, connect and remove pods.
